story.title: Jensen Huang: How the Nvidia scandal exposed the risks of Asia's big AI bet - BBC

facts.text: Jensen Huang's extraordinary return as Nvidia's boss rocked not only its shares in New York but also sent shockwaves through the artificial intelligence (AI) industry around the world.
Asia's technology industry has been under increasing pressure from the US in recent years.
The administrations of both Joe Biden and Donald Trump have tightened rules on the export of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China.
It is an indispensable engine of the company's AI dominance because of East Asia's semiconductor manufacturing and memory ecosystems," Loh says.
In the Asia-Pacific region, the data centre market, which is largely powered by Nvidia chips, is in the midst of an "unprecedented boom", according to market research group CBRE , external .
Huang said earlier this year that Nvidia plans to invest around $150bn (£114.4bn) a year in Taiwan at a launch to celebrate the firm's planned headquarters on the island.
Jensen Huang signs a Taiwanese banknote for a visitor at Computex 2026 in Taipei
Megaspeed has said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".
For economies betting heavily on AI, Nvidia has become "hugely important", with vast sums being spent on its chips and factory activity increasingly dependent on its technology, Loh told the BBC.
Nvidia's chips fill its data centres, power its AI models and feed the companies making cars and electronics.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a BBC request for comment.
In many economies, news of Huang's return to Nvidia was met with jubilation.
On top of that, Nvidia is a financial backstop and major lender to companies in the AI supply chain.
This will hit South East Asian countries, which have invested billions in data centre infrastructure to cater to Chinese firms.

Nvidia has already paused shipments to the region, according to the Financial Times, although it is unclear if this is only a temporary move while it figures out how to comply with the new export rules.
Investor concerns about the trillions of dollars being poured into AI and the pivotal role Nvidia plays in the industry were already sending tremors through global stock markets.
Trump boosts Nvidia boss return but are US politicians on board?
And as Democrats prepare to take control of the US House and Senate in the New Year, Huang is likely to face further risks.
